input.quote: Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows:
input.rationale: The Base Agreement runs for an initial three-year term (p0104) and Section 5.0 permits termination only for cause (breach, insolvency, competitor acquisition, force majeure). IBM therefore has no right to terminate the Agreement for convenience during a multi-year committed term, which the playbook treats as a missing-behaviour deviation. Exit today runs only through six months' non-renewal notice under Section 4.0 (a natural-term non-renewal, addressed under RENEWAL, not T4C) and IBM's purchase-order cancellation right in SOW Section 6.1, which reaches individual Purchase Orders only and carries cost reimbursement. On the other side, MSL has no mid-term convenience right: Section 5.1 confines termination by either Party to cause, so preferred element 4 is already met and we have not added a prohibition. We added the shortest preferred-level clause (new Section 5.4) giving IBM a 30-day convenience exit with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; 60-90 days' notice is available as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Add IBM convenience termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees as new Section 5.4
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 5.0 lets either Party exit only for cause, so across a three-year term we have no way to leave on notice. We have added a short Section 5.4 giving IBM a convenience termination right on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; if you prefer, we can move to 60-90 days' notice as our fallback.

ops.text: Termination for Convenience by IBM. IBM may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL, in which case MSL shall refund to IBM, pro rata, any fees prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
